html:
The Jaitmatang, also spelt Yaithmathang, are an Aboriginal people of the Victorian Alps, around the high plains and the valley of Omeo in northeast Victoria.

Like the Ngarigo to the northeast, they took part in the summer gatherings in the mountains to feast on bogong moths. Their neighbours were the Gunaikurnai to the south and the Waywurru and Taungurung to the west.

Squatters reached the Omeo plains in the late 1830s, and gold was found there in the 1850s. The Jaitmatang were badly hit by disease and violence, and their numbers fell sharply in the decades after contact. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Jaitmatang, also spelt Yaithmathang, are an Aboriginal people of the Victorian Alps, around the high plains and the valley of Omeo in northeast Victoria.
